summary: Bloomberg's profile of Denise George, the former US Virgin Islands attorney general who says she was fired after more than three years pursuing Jeffrey Epstein's estate, Leon Black and JPMorgan. She describes pressure from Governor Albert Bryan Jr. to settle quickly and move on, and Epstein's deep political and legal ties in the territory. The three cases brought settlements totaling over $240 million, and she was dismissed on New Year's Eve, four days after suing JPMorgan.
one_line: Fired USVI attorney general Denise George says she was pushed out after pursuing Epstein's estate, Leon Black and JPMorgan amid pressure to bury the scandal.
key_facts: Denise George, 64, was the 16th attorney general of the US Virgin Islands and was dismissed by letter on New Year's Eve, four days after she filed suit against JPMorgan.

Epstein's estate settled first, agreeing to pay $105 million plus half the proceeds from the sale of Little St. James; the settlement also included return of $80 million in tax incentives, half a million for environmental remediation, and a victims' compensation fund.
Leon Black settled with the Virgin Islands for $62.5 million last January, and JPMorgan Chase settled for $75 million in September; none of the parties admitted wrongdoing.
George was named attorney general in 2019, less than two months before Epstein was arrested at New Jersey's Teterboro Airport after flying from Paris.

Governor Albert Bryan Jr. told The St. Thomas Source: 'If we never mention Jeffrey Epstein again, that would be good for me'; his office said George's dismissal was unrelated to her pursuit of JPMorgan, though Bryan later said he couldn't have an attorney general launching lawsuits he didn't know about.
In 2019 Epstein sought a waiver loosening sex-offender restrictions, such as giving 21 days' notice before travel; George denied the request in May 2019 after Bryan texted her to make a decision.

Epstein's lawyers on the waiver request worked for Kellerhals Ferguson Kroblin, the firm that supported Bryan's campaign; Erika Kellerhals and Greg Ferguson hosted a $1,000-a-head fundraiser for Bryan in 2018.
Epstein received $300 million in tax breaks from the territory's Economic Development Commission, some while Bryan was EDC chairman; no official has been accused of wrongdoing.
Cecile de Jongh, wife of former governor John de Jongh, worked for Epstein as office manager and unofficial political emissary.
Epstein's trust in the Virgin Islands held his personal fortune, valued at $577 million at his death.

Emails in the litigation revealed Epstein's close relationship with Jes Staley, a JPMorgan banker who later ran Barclays; Staley has not been accused of wrongdoing by authorities, and his lawyers say he had no decision-making authority over Epstein's accounts.
George said: 'My bar license, my integrity were more important to me,' and that she would lose her job rather than be part of a cover-up.
Investigators met a code of silence: many Epstein employees signed nondisclosure agreements, and some alerted the estate's lawyers when investigators reached out.
